analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line edit to the `gpt_oss` row of the model-family table in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1353). The row now states that a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with scalar bounds that take the activation dtype (GPTOSS+Experts.swift, `swiglu`). That row is outside the two supplied head-text units (lines 416-1235), so I judged it from the patch excerpt. The supplied units contain no changes. They are unchanged surrounding documentation, covering Nemotron Super slot lifecycle, prefill and deadline policy, MTP, sampling defaults and streaming reasoning.

The change is documentation only. It adds no code, configuration, endpoints, keys, trust boundaries or attestation paths. It does not touch the prefix-cache security posture in T-041 (SSD tier, HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped cacheSalt), the coordinator-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), or the provider process boundary (TB-003, TB-007). No threat-model assumption is invalidated. The new text asserts a numerical-dtype property, not a security control, so it needs no threat-model update.

Limits: I did not verify the Swift source claim about `swiglu` dtype handling, because that file was not supplied. It is a numerical-behavior claim with no security impact visible in the evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract and not as a finding. Remaining integration questions: none that affect security.
